text:
ashwin: Quick sync — I'm planning a small infra change for inference-api. Proposal: convert Deployment -> StatefulSet (ordinal stability + PVC claims for cache), keep 2 replicas during low traffic (was 3), and add lifecycle.preStop TCP drain + readiness probe tweak. Also need TF change to switch serviceAccount used by secret-fetcher and add an annotation for kube-system sa. Looking for quick reviews and any gotchas.

maya: curious — why STS rather than a Deployment + stable PVC controller?

ashwin: primary reason is ordinal-backed cache directories we currently rely on. With Deployment we saw race on PVC reuse during scale down that broke warm cache restore. STS keeps stable volume per ordinal.

sam: +1 on STS for PV binding. A couple questions: what's roll out plan? RollingUpdate partition? maxUnavailable?

ashwin: planned rollout: canary to 10% (one replica in canary k8s namespace), then split 50/50, then full. Using RollingUpdate with partitioned rollout via annotation we already use for other STS. For safety set maxUnavailable: 0 and partition-based strategy. Will coordinate with canary windows.

lina: terraform part? Where will secret-fetcher SA change live? I want to review IAM binding and ensure no service interruption.

ashwin: TF change is small — we add `kubernetes_service_account.secret_fetcher` binding to the infra module and patch the deployment spec to reference the new sa. Sample snippet in branch: 

```hcl
resource "kubernetes_service_account" "secret_fetcher" {
  metadata {
    name = "secret-fetcher"
    namespace = var.namespace
    annotations = {
      "iam.gke.io/gcp-service-account" = var.gsa_email
    }
  }
}
```

and k8s patch: 

```yaml
spec:
  template:
    spec:
      serviceAccountName: secret-fetcher
      lifecycle:
        preStop:
          exec:
            command: ["/bin/sh", "-c", "sleep 5 && pkill -SIGTERM -f inference-worker || true"]
      readinessProbe:
        httpGet:
          path: /healthz
          port: 8080
        initialDelaySeconds: 5
        periodSeconds: 5
```

sam: preStop command looks okay but pkill is a bit fuzzy. Can we use `kill -SIGINT $(cat /tmp/worker.pid)` or the app's graceful shutdown hook? We want to ensure KV cache flushed.

ashwin: yep I'll switch to the pid file approach and call the app's flush endpoint first: `curl -sS http://localhost:8080/flush && sleep 2` then kill.

maya: any perf impact from reducing replicas to 2? We usually have HPA in front.

ashwin: baseline qps low during nights; HPA will scale up under load. This is just the minReplicas change. I updated HPA minReplicas to 2 in the TF plan.

lina: I'll review the TF PR tonight. One thing — rolling STS with maxUnavailable: 0 may stall if readiness probe too strict. Suggest `initialDelaySeconds: 10` and `failureThreshold: 6` for the first rollout.

ashwin: good call. I'll apply those probe changes.

ci-bot: Terraform plan for path `infra/services/inference` completed in 45s. Changes: +1 kubernetes_service_account.secret_fetcher, +1 kubernetes_stateful_set.inference-api (replacing deployment), HPA minReplicas 2 -> 2 (no change). Plan URL: https://ci.internal/pipelines/12345

sam: quick heads-up: when we create STS the PVC template will create new claims. If we want to reuse existing PVCs we need to set `volumeClaimTemplates` names to match or perform manual binding. Otherwise we may end up with orphaned PVCs.

ashwin: noted. For canary we'll let it create fresh PVCs (cache warm will be cold), for full migration we'll coordinate manual PV rename / bind with storage. I'll add a ticket in infra board.

maya: LGTM from me for the approach, ping me when you cut the canary rollout.

ashwin: thanks all — I'll make the pid/flush change, update probe timeouts, and merge TF after lina's review. Will cut canary tomorrow morning in the low-traffic window.

deploy-bot: Scheduled canary rollout for inference-api.sts to namespace `canary` at 2024-09-18T08:00:00Z (window 2h).

lina: ack, reviewing the TF PR now.

ci-bot: apply started for plan 12345 — I will post status when done.
